depicted_variant: Sacred serpent kami uncoiling from a Mount Miwa rock cave under a thunder manifestation.

visual_requirements.description: One complete snake body, single head and no limbs, manifest serpent form
Physical thunderstorm lightning as the thunder deity manifestation, no generic aura
Rock cave at Mount Miwa, with wet stone and rain

aura: The serpent form c05/c08 emerging from the rock cave c05 amid physical thunder c07/c08 conveys divine awe, with no generic luminous envelope.
artistic_choices: Select serpent manifestation, not a human form or a red arrow; do not mix plague, sacred-marriage story or modern depictions into this scene.
Ivory-grey scales with dark natural eyes are editorial palette, not a documented color or species; no horns, crest, mane, jewels, extra limbs, wings or dragon anatomy.
Close low foreshortening creates overwhelming presence without claiming giant size; no tiny trees, people or miniature cave used as size comparators.
Natural physical lightning in the thunderstorm realizes thunder association c07/c08; no glowing snake eyes, electric body or magical aura.
prompt: ONE original square premium PAINTERLY CINEMATIC Mitoloka illustration of Ōmononushi, revered kami of Mount Miwa in his documented SNAKE manifestation, emerging from his rock cave as thunder breaks. ANATOMY: ONE living sacred SERPENT, ONE natural snake head, TWO dark natural snake eyes, ONE long continuous limbless snake body in coils and ONE tapering tail. Smooth broad snake head with closed dignified mouth, natural belly scutes and fine ivory-grey dorsal scales. No horns, crown, crest, mane, beard, hair, wings, arms, legs, ornaments or human face. This is a snake god, NOT a dragon [omononushi-c05,c08]. MOMENT: UNCOIL forcefully from the dark stone cave and raise the foremost neck toward the very low viewer, broad head facing the viewer directly and inclined slightly down in solemn divine regard; nearest coil slides over wet rock into foreground, body flowing from one continuous neck through the cave coils with no duplicate snakes. No fangs, attack, snarl or evil expression. POWER: a hard real LIGHTNING FORK tears the storm sky just outside cave, lighting serpent scales and wet rock; physical thunder manifestation from c07/c08, no spell beams, magical corona, glowing eyes or electricity along body. Rain streams on stone and sprays from moving coil. SCALE & CAMERA: extremely LOW CLOSE camera just outside the rock cave; head and rising neck fill upper half, huge foreground coil by close perspective fills lower half, snake is unmistakable dominant subject. No giant-size claim: no miniature trees, buildings or people; cave edges close cropped so no scale comparison. LIGHT & WEATHER: ONE dominating white-gold LIGHTNING FLASH outside storm-lit cave, brilliant hard edges on pale scales with deep walnut-black shadows under coils, heavy physical rain outside, cave dark. SURFACE: wet overlapping irregular snake scales, broad belly scutes, slick ancient grey rock, rivulets and spray. SETTING: rock cave of Mount Miwa in Japan [c01,c05], no invented shrine inscriptions or religious iconography. MOOD: sacred awe before a powerful earthly kami, dignified and overwhelming, respectful, never monstrous evil snake or ordinary reptile wildlife portrait. The coiling emergence plus thunder must read as active divine manifestation at 200px. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, letters, logo, border, watermark; no extra heads, eyes, tails or limbs; no borrowed film/game/anime/comic designs, no nudity or gore, no victims or plague visuals; no generic aura, neon outlines, runes, energy ribbons or glowing mist. Rich tactile painterly brushwork, square composition.
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native 1254px and 200px inspected: one snake head with two natural eyes, one continuous limbless coiling serpent body emerging from dark rock cave (c05/c08), no added horns, crowns, mane or dragon anatomy. Raised neck and moving foreground coil through wet spray give active manifestation; forked physical lightning c07/c08 is background thunder, not body aura. Tight low framing makes sacred stern presence dominate at 200px without asserting giant size. Closed mouth, no evil fangs, plague, victims, symbols, text or borrowed design. All seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px and 100px downscales. I also viewed native crops of the head (2x), the eyes (3x), the neck base where the cave coil and the foreground coil meet (1.5x and 2.4x), the cave coils brightened, the rearmost coil deep in the cave (3x, brightened to rule out a hidden second head), the right edge where the coil leaves the frame, the lower-left rocks, and all four corners brightened to check for signatures. This is the documented snake manifestation (omononushi-c05 snake body; c08 manifests as a snake). It has ONE snake head with TWO natural dark eyes (no glow), two nostrils, a closed mouth, no fangs, and no horns, crest, mane, whiskers, crown or human face. The body is limbless, with no legs, wings or dragon parts. It is one continuous body with plausible occlusion. The coil from the cave runs right and twists up into the raised neck, with belly scutes turned to the viewer and the bend rounded off behind the foreground coil. The cave segment loops back into the dark to a rounded bend, with no face there. A thick foreground span sweeps from the lower-left water off the right edge. I found no Y-branch, duplicate snake or second head. The tail is out of frame, which is acceptable. It uncoils out of a wet rock cave (c05 lived in a rock cave) on a mountain (c01 Mount Miwa, habitat mountain): the near coil slides over the rock and throws spray, and the neck rears up with the head inclined down at an extremely low, close camera. That is a moment of emergence and confrontation, not a static pose. The only power effect is a real forked lightning bolt tearing the storm sky outside the cave, which also rim-lights the scales (c07 thunder god; c08 manifests as thunder). There is no aura, electricity on the body, runes or glowing mist. Heavy rain and a low-key walnut-black cave with one white-gold flash. Wet, overlapping, ivory-grey scales and slick rock; the pale colour is editorial and declared as such in artistic_choices. At 200px it reads as a huge sacred serpent rearing out of the mountain under thunder: imposing and awe-inspiring, as §6.5 asks for a living Shinto kami (Ōmiwa worship, c02/c03), not a pet or zoo reptile, and not an evil monster. No plague scene, victims, red arrow, shrine, torii or invented inscriptions; no text, signature, border or borrowed film/game/anime snake design. All seven Uji Sangar items pass. Minor issues that are not blocking: (1) the finish is near-photographic, with shallow-focus bokeh at lower left, rather than the requested painterly brushwork. This is within what was accepted for animal-form beings (for example moon-lake-monster, 2118-r03), and it is not the person-photo problem behind earlier rejections. (2) The far background shows bare, jagged crags rather than Miwa's wooded cone, but the embedded claims do not describe the mountain's look and the crags stay secondary. (3) The closed mouth line turns slightly upward, but with the low gaze and the storm it reads as solemn, not cute.
